segments.translit: tam evārthaṃ paramārthasatyasākṣātkaraṇena janārthāya siddhācāryo hi śabarapādaḥ pratipādayati—
segments.translation: The [siddha]{siddha} master [Śabarapāda]{p-sabara}, through directly realizing [ultimate]{paramartha} truth, sets out that same meaning for the sake of people:
segments.note: Munidatta introduces the last song: the siddha master Śabarapāda, having directly realized ultimate truth, sets out 'that same meaning' for the sake of people (cp.50.m1). The Tibetan comment instead reads 'the ultimate truth of reality' (de kho na nyid), taking 'that same' with the truth.

flags.note: The Tibetan translation (Toh 2293) of cp.50.m1 has de kho na nyid kyi don dam pa'i bden pa, 'the ultimate truth of reality', apparently taking tam eva ('that same') with the truth rather than with artha ('meaning'), and gsungs, 'spoke', for pratipādayati, 'sets out'. I follow the Sanskrit.

segments.translit: gaaṇata gaaṇata ityādi | gagaṇety uktidvayena śūnyātiśūnyaṃ boddhavyam | tallagnavaṭikāsandhyayā tṛtīyaṃ mahāśūnyaṃ ca | hṛdayeneti | prabhāsvaracaturthe[na] śūnyena kuṭhārikāṃ kṛtvā etadā[68]lokādiśūnyatrayasya doṣaṃ chittvā | kaṇṭheti | sambhogacakre nairātmadharmādhigamenānudinaṃ yo 'pi yogivaro jāgrati(?) tasya trailokyaṃ sughaṭaṃ bhavatīti |
segments.translation: 'In the [sky]{gagana}, in the [sky]{gagana},' and so on. By the twofold utterance '[sky]{gagana}' the empty and the [very empty]{atisunya} are to be understood; and by the [twilight language]{sandhya-bhasa} of 'the [field]{bari} attached to it', the third, the [greatly empty]{mahasunya}. 'With the [heart]{hrdaya}': having made an [axe]{axe} of the [fourth emptiness]{caturtha-sunya}, [clear light]{prabhasvara}, having cut the fault of these [three emptinesses]{sunyatraya} beginning with [light]{aloka}. 'At his [neck]{kantha}': whatever best of [yogis]{yogi} is awake day after day in the [wheel of enjoyment]{sambhoga-cakra}, through realizing the [dharma]{dharma} of [selflessness]{nairatmya}, for him the [three worlds]{trailokya} become well joined.
segments.note: Munidatta reads the doubled sky as the empty and the very empty, and the field joined to it, in twilight language, as the third, the greatly empty. 'With the heart': the fourth emptiness, clear light, made an axe that cuts the fault of the other three. The neck is the wheel of enjoyment, where the yogi wakes to selflessness (cp.50.m2).

equations.en: the empty and the very empty
the third, the greatly empty
by the fourth emptiness, clear light
an axe made of the fourth emptiness, clear light, which cuts the fault of the three emptinesses
in the wheel of enjoyment

flags.note: Shastri's folio mark [68] stands inside etadā|lokādi in cp.50.m2 and is not translated. His restoration caturthe[na] is accepted.

For etad-ālokādi-śūnyatraya, 'these three emptinesses beginning with light', the Tibetan translation (Toh 2293) of cp.50.m2 has de la bsnun pa la sogs pa stong pa gsum po'i skyon, 'the fault of the three emptinesses, striking at it and so on', as if reading a word for striking where the Sanskrit has āloka. The folio break makes the Sanskrit slightly insecure, but āloka fits the scheme of three emptinesses; I follow it.

For tallagnavaṭikāsandhyayā the Tibetan of cp.50.m2 has de la sbyar zhing bsdus pa'i rigs pas, 'by the reasoning of joining to it and combining', with no field: it takes sandhyā as a joining, not as twilight language. It then adds dang snying po, 'and heart', citing hṛdaya. Its verse line 1a has no heart (lta zhing, 'looking'), so the comment's snying po supports hṛdayena for heñce.

jāgrati(?) is printed with Shastri's query; the correct form is jāgarti, 'is awake'. The Tibetan of cp.50.m2, rab tu sad pas, 'being fully awake', confirms the sense, which also fits the song's jāgante.

sughaṭa may mean 'well joined, well formed' or 'easily accomplished'; I chose 'well joined'. The Tibetan of cp.50.m2 has de 'jig rten gsum du gsal bar byed, 'he makes it clear in the three worlds', as if reading another word.

In cp.50.m2 hṛdayena is glossed by the parallel instrumental prabhāsvaracaturthena śūnyena: the heart is the fourth emptiness, clear light, and that is made into the axe. The two gerunds (kṛtvā, chittvā) have no main verb; the song's line supplies it.

segments.translit: dhruvapadenāsaṅgaparihāraṃ karoti— chāṛa ityādi māā ityādi | viṣamadundolikāyāṃ karmāṅganāyāṃ bho yogi[n] mo[me]hatyāgena mahāmudrāsiddhiṃ kuruta | dviruktir ati(dviruktīd iti)sambhrame | tathā ca sarahapādāḥ— yāmai ityādi— ata eva śabaro hi mahāsukhena bhave śūnye nairātmajñānamudrā[ṃ] gṛhītvā vilasati krīḍati |
segments.translation: With the [refrain]{dhruvapada} he brings about the abandoning of attachment. 'Let go' and so on, '[illusion]{maya}' and so on: O [yogi]{yogi}, by giving up [delusion]{moha} about the perilous [dundolī]{dundoli}, the action-woman, bring about the [accomplishment]{siddhi} of [Mahāmudrā]{mahamudra}. The repetition expresses great urgency. And so [Saraha]{p-saraha}: 'yāmai…' and so on. Therefore the [Śabara]{sabara}, with [great bliss]{mahasukha}, in [existence]{bhava}, in [emptiness]{sunyata}, takes the [jñānamudrā]{jnanamudra} [Nairātmā]{nairatma} and is at [play]{lila}, that is, sports.
segments.note: Munidatta takes the refrain as teaching the abandoning of attachment. The perilous dundolī is the action-woman: the yogi is to give up delusion about her and accomplish Mahāmudrā; the doubled 'let go' shows urgency. Where the song has helī, his paraphrase has the jñānamudrā Nairātmā (cp.50.m3). The Tibetan comment calls the dundolī 'the one with limbs of action'.

equations.en: the action-woman (karmāṅganā)

citations.work: Saraha (Sarahapāda), a verse not identified; only its first word is quoted

flags.note: For āsaṅgaparihāra, 'abandoning attachment', the Tibetan translation (Toh 2293) of cp.50.m3 has grogs yongs su spong ba, 'abandoning companions', reading saṅga as 'company'.
Printed mo[me]hatyāgena; I read mohatyāgena, 'by giving up delusion', which the song's mohā supports.
Where the Sanskrit of cp.50.m3 has mohatyāgena, 'by giving up delusion', the Tibetan has rnal 'byor chen pos, 'by great yoga', as if reading mahāyogena.

The Tibetan of cp.50.m3 glosses its line's ma rung yan lag can, 'the wicked one with limbs', as las kyi yan lag can, 'the one with limbs of action': a calque of karmāṅganā that reads aṅganā ('woman') as aṅga ('limb').

dviruktir ati(dviruktīd iti)sambhrame: Shastri prints an alternative in brackets. I read dviruktir atisambhrame, 'the repetition is in great urgency', a grammarian's remark on chāṛu chāṛa. The Tibetan of cp.50.m3 has bdag la mtshon cha rnam pa gnyis gsungs so, apparently 'two kinds of weapon were spoken for me'; its relation to the Sanskrit is unclear.
Of Saraha's verse only the first word, yāmai, is quoted in cp.50.m3; the Tibetan renders it 'gro ba, 'going' or 'beings'. I leave it untranslated.

bhave śūnye (cp.50.m3) may be two locatives, 'in existence, in emptiness', or 'in empty existence'; the song's suṇame is 'in emptiness'. The Tibetan has bde ba chen po'i ngo bo stong pa nyid, 'emptiness whose nature is great bliss', with no existence, and takes nairātma- as selflessness (bdag med pa'i ye shes kyi phyag rgya, 'the knowledge-seal of selflessness') rather than as the goddess.
The helī of 2b is not glossed explicitly: Munidatta's paraphrase in cp.50.m3 puts the jñānamudrā Nairātmā where the song has it, so I give no equation.

segments.translit: dvitīyapadena kṛtakṛtya[tā]m āha— mama tṛtīyāvidhūtakā | khasameti guruvacanaprasādāt prabhāsvaratulyabhūtā | kapāsam iti | kakārasya pārśvavartī khakāraś caturthaśūnyaṃ mamedānīṃ sphuṭībhūtam | punar apy anyathābhāvaṃ na bhaviṣyati | tathā ca— paṛaitvā paśunā thattā nimalacānda ji[ma] sahajem̐ pharittā |
segments.translation: With the second [verse]{pada} he speaks of [having done what was to be done]{krtakrtyata}: my third, the [avadhūtī]{avadhuti}. '[Sky-like]{khasama}': by the [grace]{prasada} of the [guru's word]{guru-vacana} she has become equal to [clear light]{prabhasvara}. '[Cotton]{karpasa}': the letter kha, which stands at the [side]{parsva} of the letter ka, the [fourth emptiness]{caturtha-sunya}, has now become manifest to me. It will not become otherwise again. And so: 'Paṛaitvā paśunā thattā; like the stainless [moon]{moon}, radiant in the [innate]{sahaja}.'
segments.note: Munidatta reads couplet 3 as the poet's having done what was to be done. His field is 'my third', the avadhūtī, become equal to clear light by the guru's grace; the cotton, ka-pāsa, is 'beside ka', the letter kha, the fourth emptiness, now manifest and never to change (cp.50.m4). The Tibetan comment drops that negative.

equations.src: meri tailā bāṛī (cited as mama tṛtīyāvidhūtakā)
equations.en: my third, the avadhūtī
become equal to clear light by the grace of the guru's word
the letter kha, beside ka: the fourth emptiness, now manifest

citations.quoted: paṛaitvā paśunā thattā nimalacānda ji[ma] sahajem̐ pharittā
citations.work: an unnamed Apabhraṃśa verse (perhaps a dohā)

flags.note: Printed tṛtīyāvidhūtakā; I read tṛtīyā avadhūtikā with the Tibetan of cp.50.m4 (bdag gi gsum pa a wa d+hU tI pa), 'my third, the avadhūtī'; it could also be 'my third avadhūtī'. 'Third' seems to hear the song's tailā as tṛtīya; the Sanskrit does not quote the song's words here.
The Tibetan of cp.50.m4 first cites bdag gi ldum ra, 'my garden', and adds dben pa, 'secluded', before 'my third, the avadhūtī'.

For khasama the Tibetan of cp.50.m4 has bla ma'i zhabs kyi drin gyis 'od mtshungs par gyur pa, 'has become equal to light by the kindness of the guru's feet', where the Sanskrit has the guru's word and clear light.

The Tibetan of cp.50.m4 drops the negative: slar yang gzhan gyi ngo bo nyid du 'gyur ro, 'it will again become of another nature', against punar apy anyathābhāvaṃ na bhaviṣyati, 'it will not become otherwise again'. I follow the Sanskrit.

The Apabhraṃśa quotation in cp.50.m4 is obscure. I cannot construe paṛaitvā paśunā thattā and leave it in source form. For the second half I accept Shastri's ji[ma] and read 'like the stainless moon, radiant in the innate' (pharittā as sphuritā). The Tibetan reads dud 'gro mgon shar dri med pa'i / zla ba ji bzhin lhan skyes spro, 'the lord of beasts has risen; like the stainless moon, the innate radiates'.
For kṛtakṛtyatā the Tibetan of cp.50.m4 has bya ba byed pa, 'doing what is to be done'.

segments.translit: tṛtīyapadena tam evārthaṃ [69ka] viśeṣayati— tailā bāṛīti | tṛtīyaśūnyapārśve johnavāṭiketi jñānendumaṇḍalasyodayo yadā bhūtaḥ | tasmin samaye sakalakleśāndhakāraṃ spheṭitam iti palāyitam | ākāśeti | kaṃ sukhaṃ saṃvṛtibodhicitta[ṃ] tena yasya aṅgacinam iti |
segments.translation: With the third [verse]{pada} he specifies that same meaning. 'The [hill]{taila} [field]{bari}': at the [side]{parsva} of the third [emptiness]{sunyata}. 'The [moonlight]{moonlight} [field]{bari}': when the rising of the [moon disc]{moon-disc} of knowledge has come about. At that time the [darkness]{andhakara} of all the [afflictions]{klesa} is 'dispelled', that is, has fled. 'Sky': kaṃ is [bliss]{sukha}, [conventional]{samvrti} [bodhicitta]{bodhicitta}; that whose limbs are marked by it (aṅgacina).
segments.note: Munidatta places the field beside the third emptiness. The moonlight field is the moment the disc of the moon of knowledge rises, when the darkness of all the afflictions flees; the flowering sky he reads through kaṃ: bliss, conventional bodhicitta (cp.50.m5). The Tibetan has no line for couplet 4, yet its comment cites 'the garden's side' and 'the moon rising'.

equations.en: the third emptiness, at whose side the moonlight field lies
the rising of the disc of the moon of knowledge
fled
kaṃ: bliss, conventional bodhicitta

flags.note: Shastri's folio mark [৬৯ক] (folio 69v) stands inside the first sentence of cp.50.m5, after tam evārthaṃ; it is not translated.

aṅgacinam (cp.50.m5) is obscure: perhaps aṅgacihna, 'a mark on the limbs'. The Tibetan des gang gi yan lag tu gyur pa, 'that of which it has become a limb', seems to read something like aṅgabhūta. The sentence seems to explain ākāśa through kaṃ, bliss; my rendering is tentative.

The Tibetan translation has no verse line for couplet 4, but its comment (cp.50.m5) cites ldum ra'i rtsa ba, 'the garden's side', zla ba shar ba, 'the moon rising', and nam mkha', 'sky': the translators' text of 4a had a rising moon where the Bengali has the moonlight field spreading.
For tṛtīyaśūnyapārśve, 'beside the third emptiness', the Tibetan of cp.50.m5 has stong pa gsum pa la gnyen po, 'the remedy for the third emptiness'.
spheṭita (cp.50.m5) is Munidatta's Sanskritized form of the song's phiṭeli, glossed palāyita, 'fled'.

segments.translit: caturthasya anuśaṃsānutpādaprakṛtiprabhāsvararūpaṃ guruprasādāt yogivarasya ubhayam ekībhūya parikalpitam | ata eva saraś cittavajraḥ | śabarīti | jñānapānapramattāṃ jñānamudrāṃ gṛhītvā anāsaṅganādānandapramodena anudinaṃ kim api niścetanayate | ataḥ mahāsukhaśayyāyā[ṃ] vihvalībhūya supta iti |
segments.translation: Of the fourth: [praise]{anusamsa}. The form of [non-arising]{anutpada}, natural [clear light]{prabhasvara}: by the [guru]{guru}'s [grace]{prasada} the two, become one, are conceived by the best of [yogis]{yogi}. Therefore the [Śabara]{sabara} is the mind-vajra. '[Śabarī]{sabari}': having taken the [jñānamudrā]{jnanamudra}, [drunk]{matta} on the drink of [knowledge]{jnana}, through delight in the [joy]{ananda} of the unobstructed [nāda]{nada}, day after day he is aware of nothing at all. Therefore, overcome on the [bed]{bed} of [great bliss]{mahasukha}, he sleeps.
segments.note: Munidatta reads the millet as 'the fourth', unarisen natural clear light, in which the yogi conceives the two as one; the Tibetan comment cites it as kaM gu tsa na, without a negative. The Śabara is the mind-vajra, the Śabarī the jñānamudrā drunk on knowledge, and he lies senseless on the bed of great bliss (cp.50.m6).

equations.src: kaṅgu (cited only in the Tibetan comment, as kaM gu tsa na)
equations.en: the fourth: the form of unarisen, natural clear light
the mind-vajra
the jñānamudrā, drunk on the drink of knowledge

flags.note: The opening of cp.50.m6, caturthasya anuśaṃsā…, looks corrupt. It may hide the usual frame, 'with the fourth verse he states the praise' (caturthapadenānuśaṃsām āha), since couplet 5 is his fourth verse; or caturthasya, 'of the fourth', may gloss the millet, as the Tibetan bzhi pa, 'the fourth', suggests. The Tibetan has no 'praise' and opens by citing kaM gu tsa na. I translate literally.
Printed saraś cittavajraḥ in cp.50.m6; I read śabaraś, 'the Śabara', with the Tibetan rngon pa, 'hunter'.

The Sanskrit of cp.50.m6 does not quote the millet word. The Tibetan comment cites it as kaM gu tsa na, and its line reads kaM gu tsa ni smin gyur, 'ripened', with no negative. This supports taking the Bengali nā as part of the millet's name (kaṅgu-cīnā?) rather than 'not', as the draft does.

The Tibetan of cp.50.m6 ends de'i phyir bde ba chen pos sa wa ri ni sems med par gyur nas nyal ba'o, 'so, through great bliss, the Śabara becomes mindless and lies down', without the bed; it also adds rab tu myos pas, 'utterly drunk', to the delight of the nāda.
ubhayam ekībhūya, 'the two, become one' (cp.50.m6): the comment does not say which two, perhaps the Śabara and Śabarī of 5a.

segments.translit: pañcamapadena praveśopāyam āha— cārityādi | caturthasandhyayā caturānandā boddhavyāḥ | karmamudrāsaṅgāt | gaṛila iti yogīndreṇa sthirīkṛtāḥ | tathā cāgamaḥ— ānandās tatra jāyanta ityādi— tasyorddhe cañcālīti viṣayendriyaṃ dagdhyā sarvara iti | sakārāya paroyaṃ | ha
segments.translation: With the fifth [verse]{pada} he states the [means of entering]{pravesopaya}. 'Four' and so on: by the [fourth juncture]{caturthi-sandhya} the four [joys]{ananda} are to be understood, from association with the [karmamudrā]{karmamudra}. 'Built' (gaṛila): they are made [steady]{sthira} by the [lord of yogis]{yogindra}. And so the [scripture]{agama}: 'There the [joys]{ananda} arise,' and so on. Above it, '[pyre]{cancali}': having burned the [sense objects]{visaya} and the [senses]{indriya}. '[Śabara]{sabara}' (printed sarvara): sakārāya paroyaṃ … ha…
segments.note: Munidatta calls couplet 6 the means of entering: the 'four' are the four joys, from the karmamudrā at the fourth juncture, and 'built' (his gaṛila) means made steady by the lord of yogis. The pyre burns the sense objects and senses. His Sanskrit then breaks off mid-word (cp.50.m7); the Tibetan comment cites the pyre as gtum mo.

equations.en: the four joys, from association with the karmamudrā
made steady by the lord of yogis
having burned the sense objects and the senses

flags.note: caturthasandhyayā (cp.50.m7): 'by the fourth juncture' (sandhyā, a twilight or juncture of the day; compare the caturthī sandhyā, midnight, of song 2), or, as in tallagnavaṭikāsandhyayā in cp.50.m2, 'by the twilight language' of the word, with catur- for the song's cāri. The Tibetan has de mtshams bzhir, 'at those four junctures'. I chose 'fourth juncture'.

For gaṛila, 'built', the Tibetan of cp.50.m7 cites bskor nas, 'having encircled', as in its line (legs par bskor nas): it read the verb of 6a as 'encircle'. Munidatta's gaṛila is what the draft uses to emend bhāilārem̐ to 'built'.

For cañcālī the Tibetan comment (cp.50.m7) cites gtum mo, the caṇḍālī fire: de'i steng du gtum mo zhes pas yul dang dbang po'i phyir ro, 'above it, gtum mo: because of objects and senses', with no burning. Its line has smyug ma'i rib ma, 'bamboo wattle'.
In cp.50.m7 dagdhyā stands for dagdhvā, 'having burned', and tasyorddhe for tasyordhve, 'above it'.

From sarvara the text of cp.50.m7 is corrupt, and the manuscript breaks off mid-word after ha: here Munidatta's Sanskrit ends. sarvara is probably śabara (Tibetan sa wa ri); sakārāya paroyaṃ is obscure (the Tibetan has de byed pa'i phyir pha rol gang la stobs kyis byed pas, 'because he does that, since he acts by force on whatever other'); ha may begin haṭhena, 'by force' (stobs kyis). I leave these words in source form.

The Tibetan of cp.50.m7 goes on past the break: this is called 'drawing in' (rngub); seeing the deathlessness of the siddha master Śabarapāda, the whole host of jackals and birds weeps; and 'by this, I, Śabarapāda, … (brtsir ba, unclear)'. That continuation is not part of this Sanskrit segment and is not translated here.

segments.translit: /rkang pa drug pas rigs rdzogs par gsungs te/ bsad byas zhes pa ni yul la spro ba ste/ sems kyi rgyal po bla ma dam pa'i gsung gi ral gris mi snang bar byas nas phyogs bcu'i sangs rgyas rnams la bdag gi de kho na nyid kyis mchod par bya'o/ /de bzhin du lung las kyang / gtor ma'i mchod pa'i yo byad ni/ /gtor ma chen po dga' ba yin/ /zhes so/ /de'i phyir sa wa ri ni sems kyi rdo rje'o/ /bdag dang bdag gir 'dzin pa yongs su btang nas nges par rig par gyur pa'o/ /de lta bur gyur pa ni thog ma dang tha ma med pa'i bag chags kyi don bdag gis bsal zhing bros par gyur pa'o zhes so/ /de bzhin du sa ra ha'i zhabs kyis kyang / rtog pa rnams nyams nyams las sangs rgyas su/ /blo ngan rnams kyis rjes su ston par byed/ /bdag las de nyid blo ldan rnams kyis ni/ /cis kyang mkhas las lhag tu ster bar byed/
segments.translation: With the sixth [verse]{pada} he speaks of the completion of the family. 'Killed' means the one who delights in [sense objects]{visaya}: that is, having made the [king of mind]{king-of-mind} free of [appearance]{abhasa} with the [sword]{sword} of the true [guru]{guru}'s speech, one is to worship the [buddhas]{buddha} of the [ten directions]{dasadis} with one's own [reality]{tattva}. Likewise, from [scripture]{agama}: 'The requisite of the [bali]{bali} offering / is the great [bali]{bali}, [joy]{ananda}.' Therefore the [Śabara]{sabara} is the mind-vajra. Having wholly given up [I-making and mine-making]{ahamkara-mamakara}, he has come to certain knowledge. Having become so, 'the objects of the [habitual tendencies]{vasana}, without beginning or end, I have cleared away, and they have fled,' it says. Likewise [Saraha]{p-saraha} too: '[Buddha]{buddha}hood, from [conceptual thoughts]{vikalpa} waning and waning: / so the dull-witted teach. / That very thing the intelligent, from themselves, / give by every means, beyond the learned.'
segments.note: Munidatta's Sanskrit is lost from here: this comment on couplet 7 is the Tibetan translators' text (cp.50.m8), not his Sanskrit. It reads the one killed as the delighter in sense objects, the king of mind, cut down by the true guru's speech; the bali becomes worship of the buddhas with one's own reality, and the Śabara is the mind-vajra.

equations.en: the one who delights in sense objects

equations.src: gtor ma chen po (in the scripture quoted)
equations.en: joy
the mind-vajra

citations.quoted: gtor ma'i mchod pa'i yo byad ni/ /gtor ma chen po dga' ba yin/
rtog pa rnams nyams nyams las sangs rgyas su/ /blo ngan rnams kyis rjes su ston par byed/ /bdag las de nyid blo ldan rnams kyis ni/ /cis kyang mkhas las lhag tu ster bar byed/

flags.note: Munidatta's Sanskrit breaks off in cp.50.m7. This comment on couplet 7 (cp.50.m8) survives only in the Tibetan translation (Toh 2293): it is the Tibetan translators' text, translated here from the Tibetan, not Munidatta's Sanskrit.
rigs rdzogs pa, the framing phrase of cp.50.m8, is unclear: rigs is 'family, lineage, kind'; I render 'the completion of the family'. The Sanskrit word behind it is not known.

yul la spro ba (cp.50.m8) may be 'delighting in objects' or 'spreading out into objects'. It stands for the one killed, whom the Bengali 7a calls bhabamatta, 'drunk on existence'; the Tibetan line has only 'you killed'.

The tendencies 'cleared away and fled' in cp.50.m8 seem to gloss 7b, where the Bengali has 'Śabarahood is dispelled' and the Tibetan line srid rtsa thams cad zhig, 'all the roots of existence are destroyed'.

Saraha's verse in cp.50.m8 is obscure: nyams nyams ('waning', or 'decline'), rjes su ston pa ('teach', 'point out') and mkhas las lhag tu ('beyond the learned') are rendered literally, and the construal is tentative.

bdag gi de kho na nyid kyis (cp.50.m8): 'with one's own reality' (or 'my reality'). The bali entry calls this 'one's own suchness', but de kho na nyid is the glossary's tattva, 'reality', so I used that.

segments.translit: /dpal ldan he ru ka'i rgyud kyi rgyal po'i chu gter zab mo 'dus pa la sogs las/ /dpal ldan bla ma dam pa'i mgon gyi gsung bsrubs pa las grub pa gang zhig 'khrungs pa ni/ /dpal ldan de nyid bdud rtsi'i ro ru gyur pa rang la ston par byed pa'i mthar gnas pa/ dpal ldan de nyid dpung gnyen kyang ni rtag tu yang dag bsdus pa rnam par spyad pa rnams/ /bsdus pa de la rnam par dpyod byed pa/ /nye bar bsdus pa spyod pa'i glu brgya la/ /sems can rnams kyis byang chub rtogs bya'i phyir/ /blo gros dad ldan rnams kyis dang mdzod mdzad/ /de phyed thub pas byin gyis rnam dpyad nas/ /slob mas yang dag rtogs par bya phyir dang / /kun gyis kyang ni shes par bya ba'i phyir/ /mdzod kyi don ni rab tu gsal bar byas/ /skyes bu dam pa bshes rnams la/ /thub pas byin gyis 'grel mdzad pa'i/ /bdag gi bsod nams gang de yis/ /skyes bu dam pa rgyal gyur cig/ /spyod pa'i glu'i mdzod grub pa rnams kyi rdo rje'i glu de kho na nyid gsal bar shes pa'i skye bo rnams la slob dpon thub pas byin gyis 'grel pa mdzad pa las grub pa rnams kyi rdo rje'i glu 'grel pa dang bcas pa rdzogs so//
segments.translation: Those [siddhas]{siddha} who were born from the churning, by the speech of the glorious [lord]{natha}, the true [guru]{guru}, of the [profound]{gambhira} [ocean]{ocean} of the glorious [Heruka Tantra]{tx-heruka-tantra}, king of tantras, the Samāja and the rest; who abide at the culmination of showing themselves that glorious [reality]{tattva} become the taste of [nectar]{amrta}; and who, allies of that glorious [reality]{tattva}, always practised what was rightly gathered: examining that collection, the hundred songs of [conduct]{carya} gathered together, those of faithful intelligence made a treasury, so that beings might realize [awakening]{bodhi}. Half of it [Munidatta]{p-munidatta} examined, and so that [disciples]{sisya} might rightly realize it, and so that all might understand it, he made the meaning of the Treasury fully clear. Whatever merit is mine, [Munidatta]{p-munidatta}'s, who made the commentary for holy persons, friends: by it may holy persons become victors. The [vajra]{vajra} songs of the [siddhas]{siddha}, with commentary, from the commentary that the master [Munidatta]{p-munidatta} made on the [Caryāgītikoṣa]{tx-caryagitikosa}, the [vajra]{vajra} songs of the [siddhas]{siddha}, for people who clearly know [reality]{tattva}, are complete.
segments.note: Munidatta is named (thub pas byin, 'given by the sage') in these closing verses, which are the Tibetan translators' text, not his Sanskrit (cp.50.m9). They say the faithful made a treasury of a hundred caryā songs, of which Munidatta explained half, dedicate the merit, and end with the work's title. The translators' colophon is not included.

flags.note: These closing verses and end-title (cp.50.m9) survive only in the Tibetan translation (Toh 2293): they are the Tibetan translators' text, translated from the Tibetan, not Munidatta's Sanskrit, which breaks off in cp.50.m7. The translators' own colophon (naming Kīrticandra and Drakpa Gyaltsen) is not part of this segment.

The first stanza of cp.50.m9 is hard to construe. 'dus pa may name the (Guhya)samāja or simply mean 'gathered'; grub pa gang zhig 'khrungs pa may be 'the siddhas who were born' (my reading) or 'whatever accomplishment arose'; dpung gnyen is 'allies'; rang la ston par byed pa'i mthar gnas pa is rendered 'abide at the culmination of showing themselves'. I make the siddhas the subject of the stanza.
dad ldan rnams kyis dang mdzod mdzad (cp.50.m9): the dang is unexpected; I read 'made a treasury'.

thub pas byin, 'given by the sage', translates the name Munidatta (cp.50.m9). bdag gi bsod nams is first person, as if Munidatta speaks, though the verb mdzad is honorific. rgyal gyur cig: 'may they become victors' (jinas), or 'be victorious'.
The last sentence of cp.50.m9 is the work's end-title; the phrase 'for people who clearly know reality' might instead describe the songs.

questions: cp.50.m6 opens caturthasya anuśaṃsā…, which looks corrupt: is it the usual frame 'with the fourth verse he states the praise', or does caturthasya, 'of the fourth', gloss the millet, as the Tibetan bzhi pa suggests? I translated literally ('Of the fourth: praise') and flagged it.

cp.50.m7: should caturthasandhyayā be 'by the fourth juncture' (glossary caturthi-sandhya, used here) or 'by the twilight language' of the word 'four', on the model of tallagnavaṭikāsandhyayā in cp.50.m2?

cp.50.m7: the Tibetan goes on past the point where Munidatta's Sanskrit breaks off (the birds and jackals weep on seeing Śabarapāda's deathlessness). Should that continuation become its own Tibetan reading-text segment, as cp.50.m8 is for couplet 7?

cp.50.m2: the first of the four emptinesses, 'the empty' (śūnya), has no glossary entry, though atisunya, mahasunya and sarvasunya do. I left it unmarked. Should an entry be added to complete the set?

karmāṅganā, 'the action-woman' (cp.50.m3; also cp.21.m2 and cp.23.m4), is listed as a form of karmamudra, but 'karmamudrā' is not its literal English, so I left 'action-woman' unmarked. Should 'action-woman' become a variant of karmamudra?

cittavajra / sems kyi rdo rje, 'the mind-vajra' (cp.50.m6, cp.50.m8), matches trivajra, whose English is 'three vajras', so I left 'mind-vajra' unmarked. Add it as a variant, or as an entry of its own?
The bali entry describes the worship in cp.50.m8 as 'with one's own suchness', but de kho na nyid is the glossary's tattva, 'reality'. I used 'reality'; should the bali entry be aligned?
cp.50.m5 reads the sky of 4b through kaṃ, 'bliss, conventional bodhicitta'. Should the akasapuspa entry record this, and does kaṃ, which recurs (cp.18.m3, cp.50.m5), want an entry of its own?
cp.50.m4: I left the first half of the Apabhraṃśa quotation (paṛaitvā paśunā thattā) in source form because I cannot construe it. Is a tentative English rendering preferred?
cp.50.m2: sughaṭa rendered 'well joined'. Would 'easily mastered' read better here? The Tibetan has gsal bar byed, 'makes clear'.

Commentary-only keep-source-first-gloss terms in this unit (siddha, jñānamudrā, Mahāmudrā, karmamudrā, avadhūtī, bodhicitta, nāda, vajra) got no separate first-occurrence notes, since the weave schema has no notes field. Should their glosses go in the woven notes?
